The current top tab bar (instead of a sidebar session stack, which is standard in AI chat UIs) is prone to accidental session loss. While trying to switch to a session, I accidentally clicked the close (X) button that appears on the tab, and the entire long session was deleted with no way to recover it.

**Suggestion:** Replace the tab bar with a sidebar list of sessions, like most other AI chat interfaces use. This prevents accidental deletions and makes session management more intuitive.

Adding another data point plus a working in-place cleanup — macOS, opencode 1.18.30 (Homebrew), 9 concurrent long-running TUI sessions sharing one `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`.

**Symptom.** Launching a new session failed with the generic Bun error:

```
error: An unknown error occurred, possibly due to low max file descriptors (Unexpected)
Current limit: 2560
```

The file-descriptor hint is a red herring for this failure. Raising the limit (`ulimit -n 2147483646`) removes the hint but the same `Unexpected` remains, and a session only holds ~35–99 fds. The binary has distinct strings for `ProcessFdQuotaExceeded` / `SystemFdQuotaExceeded`; this was the generic branch.

**Measurements before cleanup:**
- DB: 3.0 GB; `event` table: 2.77 GB (~92%)
- `message.updated.1`: 31,817 rows / 2.52 GB, largest single events ~9 MB
- `message.part.updated.1`: 89,200 rows / 193 MB
- largest sessions: 364 / 354 / 333 / 309 / 185 MB of `message.updated.1` each
- cause matches #42748: each `message.updated.1` embeds the full message incl. `summary.diffs` (complete patches), re-serialized on every streaming update.

**Cleanup** (backed up first; keep only the latest snapshot per message):

```sql
SELECT id FROM (
  SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    PARTITION BY aggregate_id, json_extract(data,'$.info.id')
    ORDER BY seq DESC
  ) AS rn
  FROM event WHERE type='message.updated.1'
) WHERE rn > 1;
```

Deleted that set (23,727 rows), then `VACUUM` + `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`.

**Result:** 3.0 GB → 594 MB. `PRAGMA quick_check` = ok; all 89 sessions / 8,199 messages / 37,830 parts intact.

Two notes:
1. `VACUUM` alone did not shrink the file while the 9 sessions held the WAL; the space only came back after `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`. With concurrent writers this likely interacts with #48416 (`SQLITE_BUSY` / busy_timeout). A built-in prune should checkpoint explicitly.
2. This regrows. The upstream fix is delta storage or pruning on session completion (as #41175 proposes); an `opencode db prune` command would make it safe for users.

This is the same prune the community tool in #41175 performs — just confirming it is reproducible and surfaces as the generic `Unexpected` startup error on macOS.

## Update: Completed bash commands stuck in "running" state

Additional finding — **commands that completed successfully** are still shown as "running" by the bash tool.

### Evidence

This session (`ses_fed9937acffevoWSMgWVkObvfJ") has 6 stuck bash tool calls, all of which were **completed by the agent** during this conversation:

1. `kill -9 1090` — server restart attempt (completed)
2. `pkill -f "opencode web"` — server restart attempt (completed)
3-6. Multiple restart and database check commands (all completed)

All commands produced output and the session continued working. But the bash tool still shows them as "running".

### Key insight

This is not just about `exec` or background processes. **Any bash command** can get stuck in "running" state after completion. The bash tool's completion detection is broken.

### Impact

- UI shows "Running command..." indefinitely
- Session continues to work (can send/receive messages)
- But the stuck tool state may eventually cause the session to become unresponsive
- This happened in the session currently being used to document this bug

### Affected interface

User is using OC Remote interface app. May be relevant to how the interface detects command completion.

Independent confirmation of this fix on **macOS arm64**, which I think is the platform gap left by the verification above (Linux x64/glibc).

I hit #48372 after a routine `brew upgrade` to 1.18.30 and debugged it from scratch before finding this PR; I landed on the same root cause and an equivalent patch, so this is a genuinely independent reproduction rather than a re-run of the same steps.

### Environment

- macOS 15 (Darwin 25.6.0), arm64
- Bun 1.4.2
- `dev` at `95daf90`

### The undefined dependency is directly observable

Rather than driving a full prompt, the bad dependency can be observed at the graph level. Forcing the hazardous evaluation order (search before filesystem) and bundling is enough:

```ts
import "./src/filesystem/search"
import { FileSystem } from "./src/filesystem"
const deps = (FileSystem.node as any).dependencies
console.log(deps.map((d: any) => d?.name ?? "<UNDEFINED>"))
```

```
bun build ./probe.ts --target=bun --outfile=probe.js && bun run probe.js
```

Before (unpatched `dev`):

```
[ "@opencode/FileSystem", "@opencode/Location", "<UNDEFINED>" ]
```

With this PR's `search.ts` change applied:

```
[ "@opencode/FileSystem", "@opencode/Location", "@opencode/v2/FileSystem/Search" ]
```

That `<UNDEFINED>` is what later reaches `resolve` in `layer-node.ts`:

```ts
{ cache, resolve: (node) => replacementMap.get(node.name) ?? node }
```

`node.name` on the undefined entry is the minified `a.name` in the reported stack.

Note this only manifests **bundled**. Run from source, the same cycle throws the much clearer `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'node' before initialization` — which is likely why it escaped pre-release testing.

### Also checked, with this PR applied

- `tsc --noEmit -p packages/core` — exit 0
- `bun test packages/core/test/filesystem/` — 36 pass, 0 fail

### This appears to be the only instance of the pattern

Since the failure class is "a `deps:` array read at module-eval time references a namespace imported from a cycle partner", I scanned for other occurrences: build the runtime import graph (excluding `import type`), find modules whose top-level `deps: [...]` dereferences `X.node`, and flag those where `X` is mutually reachable with the module.

Across 669 modules under `packages/core/src` and `packages/opencode/src`, that reports exactly one hazard — `filesystem.ts` → `filesystem/search.ts` — and zero once this patch is applied. So the targeted fix looks complete rather than one instance of a wider pattern.

### Possible lighter-weight regression test

The bundle probe above needs no provider, credentials, network, or session, and runs in about a second. It may be worth considering alongside (or instead of) the full compiled runner, since it asserts the actual invariant — no `undefined` in a compiled layer graph — and would catch any future reintroduction of this cycle anywhere in the graph, not just this module pair.

A related thought for a separate change: `LayerNode.compile` could validate dependencies and throw `undefined dependency in node <name>` instead of dereferencing `.name`. That would have turned this into a one-line diagnosis rather than a silent `Unexpected server error`. Happy to open that separately if it would be useful.

### Impact

Worth noting this is a full outage on the affected build — every prompt fails before any provider request, and the surfaced error is a generic `Unexpected server error`, so it reads as an auth or provider problem. Several people in #48372 understandably suspected their credentials first. Pinning to 1.18.29 is an effective workaround in the meantime.

Thanks for splitting this out. I agree with the scope: this improves diagnosis of #48372; #48397 is still needed to remove the filesystem/search runtime cycle. Checking at construction also makes sense for attributing the captured undefined dependency to its owning node.

One gap in the structural-node backstop, from reading `e947236e`: `compile` calls `flatten(root)` before its new check, and `node.dependencies.flatMap(flatten)` recursively expands groups without validating their dependencies. A hand-built group therefore bypasses the guard:

```ts
const badGroup: LayerNode.Node<never> = {
  kind: "group",
  name: "external-group",
  // @ts-expect-error Deliberately malformed dependency
  dependencies: [undefined],
}
LayerNode.compile(badGroup)
```

Here `flatten` reaches `undefined.kind` rather than the named dependency error; the same applies when that group is nested under an otherwise valid layer. Could you validate group dependencies before recursively flattening them, and add root/nested hand-built-group tests alongside the hand-built-layer test?

This is a source-review finding, not an independent run of your suite or a new platform-validation claim. The normal `make`/`group` construction checks do cover the reported filesystem case.

Thanks for the detailed report. This is package/runtime version skew rather than malformed SSE.

`0.0.0-beta-17823` bundles `effect@4.0.0-rc.110`, while configuring `@opencode/ai@2.0.3` loads `effect@4.0.0-rc.112`. Those versions use incompatible internal Scope layouts, so the older runtime attempts `scope.state.finalizers.set(...)` on a newer Scope where `finalizers` can be undefined. We reproduced the exact crash with the same valid SSE fixture under rc.110; it succeeds when the runtime and provider both use rc.112.

Please replace the retired beta package with the current stable CLI:

```sh
npm uninstall -g @opencode-ai/cli
npm install -g @opencode/cli@latest
```

No SSE or provider-side workaround is required.

Confirming the same `temperature` bootstrap failure on Windows 11 Enterprise. Still reproducible on **1.18.30** (and **1.17.19**); downgrading to **1.14.51** only partially mitigates it.

## Environment

- OpenCode Desktop (Windows x64)
- OS: Windows 11 Enterprise `10.0.26100`
- Affected builds: **1.18.30** (latest at the time) and **1.17.19**
- Partially-working build: **1.14.51** (existing projects load, but startup still briefly shows `Could not reach Local Server. Retrying automatically...`)
- `opencode.db`: ~690 MB, shared with a running CLI instance
- Host environment that plausibly slows the renderer's first fetch: locked-down corporate machine, **Cloudflare WARP** running, **KakaoTalk AdGuard** (WFP-based), and a system **PAC auto-config** proxy.

## Symptoms

- On launch the UI shows `Could not reach Local Server. Retrying automatically...` (`app.server.retrying`), and on 1.17.19/1.18.30 existing projects would not load.
- Renderer log repeatedly shows:

```text
[2026-09-13 23:20:42.143] [error] Failed to finish bootstrap instance TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'temperature')
[2026-09-13 23:20:43.669] [error] Failed to finish bootstrap instance TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'temperature')
[2026-09-13 23:23:13.833] [error] Failed to finish bootstrap instance TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'temperature')
```

and occasionally:

```text
[2026-09-11 16:52:51.163] [error] Failed to finish bootstrap instance ClientError: UnsupportedContentType
[2026-09-11 16:53:08.292] [error] Failed to finish bootstrap instance ClientError: UnsupportedContentType
```

- The **main process** reports the sidecar ready in ~2 s while the renderer is still failing, e.g.:

```text
[2026-09-13 23:20:10.754] [info] spawning sidecar { url: 'http://127.0.0.1:59683' }
[2026-09-13 23:20:14.931] [info] server ready   { url: 'http://127.0.0.1:59683' }
```

so this looks like the renderer-side detection race, not a dead server.

- Server Management lists the built-in connection as **"Local Server"** with its version rendered as `local` (i.e. shown as `vlocal`).

## Version regression

- **1.14.51**: no (or far less) bootstrap failure; connection recovers.
- **1.17.19 / 1.18.30**: reproducible `temperature` bootstrap error + `Retrying automatically...`, projects fail to load.

This corroborates @ssc-esiemiat's analysis of the 5 s timeout in `detectServerProtocol()` and a slow Chromium cold start: on a locked-down corporate Windows machine (large CA store, WARP, AdGuard/PAC proxy), the renderer's first request to the sidecar can exceed the probe timeout, the client falls back to `"v2"`, and the downstream `/api` calls yield empty providers and the `temperature` crash.

Happy to provide full `renderer.log` / `main.log` archives if useful.

Thanks for the thorough dig. None of this can happen in V2: each turn gets its own publisher, a second step-finish dies, and SessionUsage.add already handles the spots that do fold steps.

This issue targets the V1 processor though (packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts), which is still what ships. The overwrite is still there on current dev: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/95daf90670b7c039c436c85537da5fbfe2205b41/packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts#L458-L459

In V1 the prompt loop reuses one assistant message across steps, so `cost +=` and `tokens =` drift apart once a turn has multiple step-finishes.

Also agreed SessionUsage.add isn't the right fold here as-is, it sums input and cache.read too. #42326 only accumulates output/reasoning/cache.write and keeps the final step's input/cache.read instead.

Can retitle with a (v1) prefix if that makes triage easier.

Same root cause as #43557: after a restart, OpenCode replays the stale `reasoning.encrypted_content` blob (bound to the previous caller/key) and upstream rejects it with `not issued to this caller`. New chats work because they carry no stale blob.

I wrote a shim plugin that strips blobs older than the current server process before each request, keeping text summaries: https://github.com/unurgunite/opencode-sanitize-reasoning

On the affected Windows machine, `opencode.global.dat` started with a UTF-8 BOM (`EF BB BF`). The rest of the file was valid JSON, but electron-store passes the decoded `U+FEFF` straight to `JSON.parse`, so the store could no longer be read.

This was hard to notice because `store-get` catches the error and returns `null`, while `store-set` rejects. In my case the model visibility toggles worked until restart, and `renderer.log` showed the same `SyntaxError` for every write.

Removing only the BOM fixed it. The existing values loaded again, and the next write rewrote the file without the BOM.

I checked the current `dev` branch at `95daf906`: `store.ts` still uses the default deserializer, and the `store-get` / `store-set` behavior is unchanged. I also couldn't find an existing report or PR for this specific BOM case.

Good catch — confirmed and fixed in `ee2a499`. Your reading was exactly right: `flatten` expanded groups before the check ran, so both the root and nested hand-built cases hit `undefined.kind` rather than the named error.

Chasing it turned up a third instance of the same class that neither of us had flagged, and it was the one that mattered.

### `rewriteReplacementDependencies` was reproducing the original error on the production path

It walks the graph independently of `walk`, and `hoist` reaches it directly for tagged nodes — the tagged branch stores the node via `rewriteReplacementDependencies` and returns `group([])` without calling `context.visit`, so the whole subtree was only ever traversed by that unguarded recursion. An undefined entry there gave:

```
TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'node.name')
```

which is the original #48372 signature, unchanged.

This is not hypothetical. `location-services.ts:96` hoists with `allReplacements = replacements.concat([[Location.node, Location.boundNode(ref)]])`, which is never empty, so `rewriteReplacementDependencies` skips its `size === 0` early return and always runs. Without a check there, the headline claim of this PR was false for anything under a `global`-tagged node. Now validated in that recursion too, with a regression test that fails if the check is removed.

### Two smaller things from the same pass

- `checkDependencies` called `findIndex` unconditionally, so a node with no `dependencies` field went from tolerated to throwing an undiagnostic `TypeError` — the exact error class this PR exists to remove, emitted by the guard itself. A missing array is now treated as nothing to check.
- `=== undefined` let `null` through to die later in `flatten`; it now rejects both.

I also reworded the comment on the `walk` check. It claimed every visitor maps `recur` over the dependencies, which is untrue for tagged and unbound nodes — that inaccuracy is precisely what hid the rewrite gap.

### On sequencing

Building the binary surfaced something worth stating explicitly, and I have added it to the PR description: **this should not merge ahead of #48397.** With that cycle still present, the guard fires during startup, so the compiled binary fails on every command including `--version`, and `script/build.ts` fails its own smoke test. Verified both ways on macOS arm64 — guard alone on current `dev` fails the smoke test; guard plus your `search.ts` change builds, passes the smoke test, and completes a real prompt.

### Verification

- `packages/opencode` 3584 pass / 22 skip / 0 fail; `packages/core` 1105 pass / 0 fail
- The real `locationServices` graph (36 top-level nodes) hoists with replacements and compiles cleanly, so the guard does not false-positive on the shipped graph
- Repo-wide `bun typecheck` 30/30; `oxlint` unchanged from baseline on the touched files; `prettier --check` clean
- `schema`, `enterprise` and `sdk-next` have failures that are byte-identical with and without this change, so they are pre-existing

opencode v1.18.30: SystemPrompt.environment crashes with TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'a.name')                                                  

### Description

opencode v1.18.30 crashes when building the system prompt environment. The error occurs in the embedded v2 model catalog resolution code during nested .map() iterations, where an array element is undefined but the code expects an object with a .name property.

> This makes opencode completely unusable — any prompt submission fails with:
> ▎ Failed to send prompt
> ▎ Unexpected server error. Check server logs for details.

The error is not caused by user configuration, plugins, cache, or project state. It reproduces from any directory, even with --pure (no external plugins).

### Stack trace (from ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log)

```bash
  TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'a.name')
      at resolve (/$bunfs/root/chunk-36bwgd4p.js:2:1659)
      at a (/$bunfs/root/chunk-36bwgd4p.js:2:936)
      at map (native:1:11)
      ...
      at SystemPrompt.environment (/$bunfs/root/chunk-y88jw4qv.js:50:13096)
```

### Reproduction

```
# Confirm version
opencode --version
# Expected: 1.18.30

# Reproduce the crash (no project or config needed)

opencode debug v2 --pure
# Output: Error: Unexpected error — undefined is not an object (evaluating 'a.name')
```

```
opencode --version  # should now show 1.18.29
```

- macOS Darwin 25.6.0
- Regression introduced between v1.18.29 and v1.18.30

Not a duplicate from our side — the distinct angle here is concurrency between multiple opencode instances, plus a concrete fix:

- #42304 is about EBUSY on encrypted APFS volumes (file-handle/volume semantics). Nothing here involves APFS or EBUSY.
- #42597 describes the symptom class (stall + `index.lock` deadlock after a crash). This report adds the root cause for the concurrent case and the failure-handling gaps behind the silent-outage variant:
  - snapshot locking is a process-local `Map<gitdir, Semaphore>`, while the snapshot gitdir lives on disk at `~/.local/share/opencode/snapshot/<project>/<worktree-hash>` and is shared by every opencode process in the same worktree — so independent instances race `git add` / `git rm --cached` / `git write-tree` (reproduced: 56/64 failures for each of those commands across 8 processes x 8 rounds);
  - `stage()` swallowed nonzero exits, `drop()` ignored failures, and `write-tree` output was never validated, so collisions/setup failures degraded into `tracking hash=""` — we hit a real 9-day outage caused by one 0-byte lock left behind by a killed process.
- Fix is up as #48849: cross-process serialization of the whole snapshot transaction, fail-closed + validated tree IDs, bounded retry only for the exact `index.lock` error (never deleting native locks; a stuck one now logs path/age/remedy), dead-owner recovery for our own transaction token, and revert aborts on failed restore.

If maintainers want the ~1min snapshot stall on large workspaces from #42597 handled together, I can fold that into the same effort.

Also affected on macOS. I ran an A/B plus a build-to-build comparison that narrows this down further, so posting the data here since this is the "regression" issue.

## 1. The regression window is exactly one release: 1.18.29 → 1.18.30

Same machine, same `~/.config/opencode`, same directory, back to back:

| Version | Result |
|---|---|
| 1.18.29 (`opencode-darwin-arm64@1.18.29`, unpacked to a temp dir, not installed) | ✅ prompt completes normally |
| 1.18.30 (Homebrew bottle `1.18.30_1`) | ❌ `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'a.name')` |

So it is not "somewhere between 1.18.18 and 1.18.30" — 1.18.29 is good and 1.18.30 is bad.

## 2. It is unconditional on the CLI build

Every one of these crashes identically, all with `--pure`:

| Config | Directory | Result |
|---|---|---|
| my real config | non-git dir | crash |
| my real config | git repo | crash |
| stock `{"$schema":"https://opencode.ai/config.json"}` + fresh `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`XDG_DATA_HOME` | non-git dir | crash |
| stock + fresh XDG | git repo | crash |

Ruled out: plugins (`--pure`), MCP servers, LSPs, git vs non-git, and the `references` block from #48809 (mine is commented out). `opencode agent list --pure` does **not** crash for me — only the prompt path does, i.e. `SystemPrompt.environment`.

## 3. The bun-compiled binary is affected; the Electron build of the *same* 1.18.30 is not

This looks like the most useful datapoint. I have both installed:
